jd:
Thermal systems / industrial heat-pump engineer
Junior to mid
Industrial decarbonization consultancy. Engineers design high-temperature heat pumps that upgrade waste heat from refrigeration plant cooling towers into pressurized hot water for food-processing pasteurization and CIP, document heating COP in SI W/W, and compare real machines to an ideal reverse Carnot heat-pump benchmark for design reviews and client reports.

Day to day:
- Build thermodynamic state-point tables for industrial vapor-compression heat pumps from design temperatures and refrigerant data
- Look up refrigerant properties from tables, software, or online tools and document the source
- Calculate heating effect, compressor work, and heating COP including compression efficiency
- Compare cycle performance to a reverse Carnot heat pump based on external source and delivery water temperatures
- Write clear calculation notes a senior engineer can review without guessing assumptions

Required skills:
- Can define evaporator, compressor, condenser, and expansion states for a simple vapor-compression heat-pump cycle
- Comfortable reading R1233zd(E) (or similar HCFO) thermodynamic properties from tables or property software
- Can apply isentropic and actual compression work with a given compression efficiency
- Understands heating COP (q_cond / w_comp, W/W) and the reverse Carnot heat-pump benchmark from external fluid temperatures

Nice to have:
- Familiarity with CoolProp, REFPROP, or manufacturer property software
- Experience with p-h diagrams and suction-line superheat conventions
- Prior industrial heat-pump or process-heat recovery design work

Constraints:
- Assessment is a thermodynamics calculation work sample — not building production software
- Candidates may use any tools they like for refrigerant properties and arithmetic
- Do not require paid licensed software beyond what is freely available on the desktop or online
- Starter files on the desktop are shared scenery (parameters and a blank calculation template), not a solved answer
prompt: You are checking the thermodynamic performance of an industrial high-temperature heat pump using R1233zd(E). The machine upgrades waste heat from a refrigeration plant cooling-tower loop into pressurized process hot water. Design data are fixed below. Produce a clear calculation of heating COP (q_cond / w_comp, W/W), then compare that COP to an ideal reverse Carnot heat pump based on the external waste-heat source water temperature and the process delivery water temperature. You are free to use any tools you like (spreadsheets, calculators, CoolProp/REFPROP, ASHRAE or manufacturer tables, online property tools, etc.) to obtain R1233zd(E) properties — document which source you used.
